---
title: "Choosing UMAP parameters"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 110
)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggumap)
```

This article shows how the main parameters of `stat_umap()`, `geom_umap()`
and `umap_embed()` change an embedding. The data has nested structure: three
groups, each made of three clusters of different spread.

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
groups <- matrix(rnorm(3 * 20, sd = 12), 3)
clusters <- groups[rep(1:3, each = 3), ] + matrix(rnorm(9 * 20, sd = 4), 9)
label <- rep(1:9, each = 150)
x <- clusters[label, ] + matrix(rnorm(length(label) * 20, sd = rep(c(0.5, 1, 2), each = 150)), ncol = 20)
df <- data.frame(x, group = factor(LETTERS[(label - 1) %/% 3 + 1]), cluster = factor(label))
```

## `n_neighbors` and `min_dist`

`n_neighbors` sets the size of the neighbourhood that UMAP tries to preserve.
Small values focus on fine, local structure; large values on the global
arrangement. `min_dist` controls how tightly points may be packed: small
values give dense clumps, large values a more even spread.

```{r grid, fig.height = 7}
grid <- expand.grid(n_neighbors = c(5, 15, 50), min_dist = c(0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 0.99))
embeddings <- Map(
  function(k, d) {
    emb <- umap_embed(df, starts_with("X"), n_neighbors = k, min_dist = d, seed = 1)
    cbind(emb, df[c("group", "cluster")], n_neighbors = k, min_dist = d)
  },
  grid$n_neighbors, grid$min_dist
)
embeddings <- do.call(rbind, embeddings)

ggplot(embeddings, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(
    vars(n_neighbors), vars(min_dist),
    scales = "free", labeller = label_both
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
  theme_umap()
```

Within a plot, you would write each of these as a single layer, e.g.

```r
ggplot(df, aes(colour = group)) +
  geom_umap(features = starts_with("X"), n_neighbors = 50, min_dist = 0.5)
```

## Distance metrics

`metric` defines distances in the input space. Cosine and correlation
distances ignore the magnitude of the feature vectors, which is useful for
text embeddings, counts and other data where only the direction matters.

```{r metrics, fig.height = 3.2}
metrics <- c("euclidean", "manhattan", "cosine", "correlation")
by_metric <- do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, function(m) {
  emb <- umap_embed(df, starts_with("X"), metric = m, seed = 1)
  cbind(emb, df["group"], metric = m)
}))
ggplot(by_metric, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(metric), nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
  theme_umap()
```

## Flavour and initialisation

`flavour = "0.5"` (the default) reproduces the classic umap-learn pipeline:
a spectral initialisation followed by stochastic gradient descent.
`flavour = "0.6"` uses umap-learn 0.6's recursive initialisation and the Adam
optimiser; it is faster and deterministic for a fixed number of threads.
`init` overrides the initialisation of either flavour.

```{r flavours, fig.height = 5.5}
combos <- expand.grid(flavour = c("0.5", "0.6"), init = c("auto", "pca", "random"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
by_flavour <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(f, i) {
  emb <- umap_embed(df, starts_with("X"), flavour = f, init = i, seed = 1)
  cbind(emb, df["group"], flavour = f, init = i)
}, combos$flavour, combos$init))
ggplot(by_flavour, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(vars(flavour), vars(init), scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
  theme_umap()
```

## Scaling

UMAP uses the features as they are. When they are measured in different units,
the feature with the largest range dominates the distances. `scale = TRUE`
standardises every feature first.

```{r scaling, fig.height = 3.2}
penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins
p <- ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species)) + theme_umap()
patch <- list(
  p + geom_umap(features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE) + ggtitle("scale = FALSE"),
  p + geom_umap(features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) + ggtitle("scale = TRUE")
)
has_patchwork <- requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)
if (has_patchwork) {
  patchwork::wrap_plots(patch, guides = "collect")
} else {
  for (pl in patch) print(pl)
}
```

## Advanced settings

`umap_control()` holds the remaining parameters of the algorithm. The most
useful are `repulsion_strength` (how strongly unrelated points repel each
other) and `negative_sample_rate` (how many repulsive samples are drawn per
attractive one).

```{r control, fig.height = 3.2}
strengths <- c(0.25, 1, 4)
by_strength <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strengths, function(s) {
  emb <- umap_embed(df, starts_with("X"), seed = 1, control = umap_control(repulsion_strength = s))
  cbind(emb, df["group"], repulsion_strength = s)
}))
ggplot(by_strength, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(repulsion_strength), labeller = label_both, scales = "free") +
  theme_umap()
```
